title: Emotional blunting with antidepressant treatments: A survey among depressed patients
authors: Goodwin GM, Price J, De Bodinat C, Laredo J
population: 669 adults with depression taking antidepressants and 150 recovered controls in an internet survey using the Oxford Questionnaire on the Emotional Side-Effects of Antidepressants
funder: Funding statement in the full text not read: the archived publisher page shows only the abstract. Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata list Servier and the Wellcome Trust (098461MA) as funders, and two of the four authors are affiliated with the Institut de Recherches Internationales Servier.
result: Emotional blunting was reported by 46% of treated patients (52% of men, 44% of women), without a difference between antidepressants, apparently less often with bupropion. Blunting scores correlated with depression scores (r=0.521), yet patients with low depression scores also scored higher than recovered controls (35.07 against 25.73). Among patients with blunting, 37% perceived it negatively. Self-reported, cross-sectional, without a drug-free comparison group of depressed patients.
